_meta.project: instex round 7: FLWO 1.5 m Tillinghast / FAST (id fast)
_meta.rule: Every value carries source key, location and a verbatim quote from a saved document; DERIVED, EFFECTIVE, INFERRED, SCHEMATIC as defined in data/presets_research.md; quote check counts in quote_check.

F98.cite: Fabricant, D., Cheimets, P., Caldwell, N. & Geary, J. 1998, PASP 110, 79, "The FAST Spectrograph for the Tillinghast Telescope" (bibcode 1998PASP..110...79F; 7 pp., IOP publisher PDF obtained through the ADS link gateway). The PDF text layer renders the degree sign as the digit 7, the minus sign as 2, the prime as 9, the double prime as 0, the micro sign as m and the exponent -1 as 21 (e.g. "mm21", "357" = 35 deg, "39" = 3 arcmin, "10 .5" = 1.5 arcsec); quotes below are given as extracted and each such case is read in the Notes.

M20.cite: Mink, J., Brown, W. R., Chilingarian, I. V., Fabricant, D., Kurtz, M. J., Moran, S., Rhee, J., Tokarz, S. & Wyatt, W. F. 2020, arXiv:2012.03470v1 (7 Dec 2020), "Center for Astrophysics Optical Infrared Science Archive I. FAST Spectrograph". Preprint as saved (journal reference not checked).

parameters.note: Approximate ("~77"); "mm" is the extraction of micrometers. The spherical primary has R = 27625.33 mm (Table 2, sign lost), i.e. f/9.06; the Cassegrain system is slower.

parameters.value: 8.5 (off-axis angle gamma of the parent parabola)
quotes: A collimator off-axis angle of 87 .5 allows sufficient clearance between the slit assembly and the grating
parameters.derived: Extraction "87 .5" = 8.5 deg (7 = degree sign). Check with the quoted Schroeder blur b = 0.05 g v, v = half slit length = 1.5 arcmin ("19 .5" = 1.5 arcmin): b = 0.05 x 8.5 x 1.5 = 0.64", quoted 0.6". The 8.5 deg is the angle between the parent axis and the ray to the segment center; the chief ray is deviated by that angle, so the mirror normal is tilted by half of it (4.25 deg) from the incoming chief ray (INFERRED, same convention as the DEIMOS preset). Whether F98 means the deviation or the mirror tilt is not stated.

parameters.value: OFF-AXIS (slit is NOT in the returning beam)
quotes: allows sufficient clearance between the slit assembly and the grating
parameters.note: Verdict for the colTilt gate: off-axis; the beam leaves the collimator 8.5 deg from the incoming ray and the slit assembly clears the grating. Fig. 1 of F98 shows the slit plate at the top and the collimator mirror at the bottom with the grating beside the slit plate.

quotes: FAST has three reflection gratings: a 300 line
blazed at 4750 Å, plus a 1200 line mm−1 grating blazed at 5700 Å
parameters.derived: Blaze angle (not published), first order, psi = 35 deg: sin(theta_B) = G lambda_B / (2 cos 17.5 deg): 300 l/mm 4.28 deg, 600 l/mm 8.59 deg, 1200 l/mm (5700 A) 21.0 deg. DERIVED.

parameters.value: 128 x 154 (oversized)
35 (design value used for Table 1)
parameters.derived: Extraction "357" = 35 deg. It is the design assumption of the Table 1 comparison, not stated as the as-built value; it is confirmed by three published numbers. With psi = 35 deg and f_cam = 331 mm: 300 l/mm centered 5500 A gives alpha = 22.5, beta = 12.5 deg, dispersion 1.475 A/px (Table 7: 1.47), anamorphic cos(alpha)/cos(beta) = 0.947, pupil anamorphism 1.056 (F98 Sec. 3.5.1: 1.06); 1200 l/mm at 6563 A (Table 5B center): pupil anamorphism 1.334 (published 1.33). 600 l/mm at 5500 A: 0.749 A/px (0.75); 1200 l/mm at 5500 A: 0.377 A/px (0.38). All DERIVED here.

parameters.value: alpha 22.5, beta 12.5 (diffraction), tilt 5.0 deg from the bisector, at 5500 A
parameters.derived: sin(alpha)+sin(beta) = G lambda = 0.3/um x 0.55 um = 0.165; alpha = 17.5 + 4.96, beta = 17.5 - 4.96 deg (alpha > beta; the grating is tilted off the bisector by 4.96 deg). Grating tilt for other centers: M20 Appendix A.

Order-sorting filter details (M20: "Blocking filters are available but in practice never used")

Collimator off-axis geometry in the plane of the dispersion: F98 does not say whether the 8.5 deg off-axis lies in or across the dispersion plane (Fig. 1 suggests the slit-collimator axis and the collimated beam both lie in the box plane; INFERRED)
conflicts: Slit widths: F98 Sec. 7 gives 1.0 arcsec (extracted "10") for the narrowest slit, M20 gives 1.1 arcsec. M20 is the later document; the web pages could not be checked.
Resolution with the 1.5" slit and 300 l/mm: F98 abstract says 3 A at "4000 A" coverage; Table 7 numbers give 3.6 A and 3940 A coverage.
Blaze of the 300 and 600 l/mm gratings: F98 "~4800 A", M20 4750 A.
Peak throughput: 26% (F98, 1996, telescope optics dirty) vs ~35% (M20, after primary re-aluminization).
Collimated beam: F98 abstract and Sec. 3.1 "~100 mm" vs Sec. 3.4 93 mm (the 93 mm is the as-designed value from the 963 mm parent and is used).
CCD format: 2688 x 512 (F98, FAST3) vs 2720 x 512 (FAST1, FAST2 per M20 Table 2).
Camera focal length: 350 mm (spherical mirror, Table 1/Table 4 R = 700 mm) vs effective 331 mm (Sec. 3.5.1); the effective value matches the demagnification 2.91 and the dispersions.
